what: The Spell Checker finds spelling mistakes in your text and suggests corrections. It works in twelve languages and dialects: English (US and UK), Spanish, French, German, Portuguese (Brazil and Portugal), Italian, Dutch, Russian, Turkish and Indonesian.

It uses Hunspell, the same open-source spell checker used by LibreOffice, Firefox and many other programs, running in your browser through WebAssembly together with the open dictionaries made by each language community.
Nothing is uploaded: the dictionary for your language downloads once, and your text is checked on your own device.
uses: Check an important email, cover letter or post before you send it.
Spot misspellings when you write in Spanish, French, German or another language you are learning.
Paste text from a document or form to catch typos that slipped through.
Check product descriptions, page titles and blog posts in several languages.
Proofread homework and essays without installing anything.
tutorial: Choose your language from the list. The page starts with your browser language when a dictionary for it exists.
Type or paste into Your text. The first time you use a language, its dictionary (about 0.2 to 2.3 MB) downloads; after that your browser keeps it.
Press Check spelling. With Check as I type ticked, the text is checked again a moment after you stop typing.
Possible mistakes are underlined in red in the box below and listed as chips with how often they appear.
Click an underlined word. Pick a suggestion to replace it; if the word appears more than once, Replace all fixes every copy. The next mistake opens automatically.
Press Ignore for a word that is fine in this text, or Add to my dictionary for names and terms you use often. Added words are remembered in this browser.
Press Copy text to copy the corrected text.
features: The well-known open-source spell checker, compiled to WebAssembly and run in a background worker so the page never freezes.
English US and UK, Spanish, French, German, Portuguese (Brazil and Portugal), Italian, Dutch, Russian, Turkish and Indonesian, downloaded only when needed.
Suggestions take capital letters into account, so a mistake at the start of a sentence gets capitalised suggestions.
Skips what is not a word
Web addresses, email addresses, @names, #hashtags and, if you like, words in capitals or with numbers are not checked.
Words you add are saved only in your browser and accepted in every language.
Checks long documents with hundreds of thousands of words in a second or two.

example.title: Fixing an email in English
example.text: Paste: I recieve alot of emails every day. Press Check spelling: recieve and alot are underlined. Click recieve and choose receive; then click alot. If your company name, say Zentrix, is underlined, press Add to my dictionary so it is never flagged again.

tips: Choose English (UK) for colour and organise, English (US) for color and organize.
Proper names are often unknown; add the ones you use often to your dictionary.
A word that is spelled right but wrong for the sentence, like there instead of their, is not flagged. Read your text once more.
Untick Ignore words in CAPITALS to check headings written in capitals too.
Use Next mistake to step through the text quickly.
problems: Check your internet connection and press Check spelling again. The first download needs a connection; later visits work from your browser cache.
It may be a name, a new word or a regional spelling. Press Ignore, or add it to your dictionary.
The word is too far from any dictionary word. Edit it in the text box; the check updates by itself.
They are stored in this browser. Clearing site data, private windows or another device start with an empty dictionary.
